Acceptable Usage Policy


                             

This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change at
                                any time as per the company policy.

           Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
          Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

1. Purpose
The purpose of this Acceptable Usage Policy (AUP) is to define the acceptable use of FiftyFive
Technologies's information systems, including but not limited to computers, networks, email, internet
access, and any related resources. This policy aims to protect the integrity, confidentiality, and
availability of these systems.



2. Scope
This policy applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporary workers, and other
individuals at FiftyFive Technologies who have access to or use the company’s information systems.



3. General Use and Ownership
    •   FiftyFive Technologies provides various technology resources to employees for business use.
        These resources include, but are not limited to, computers, mobile devices, software, email,
        and internet access.
    •   All data created on FiftyFive Technologies systems is the property of FiftyFive Technologies.
        Employees should have no expectation of privacy when using company resources.
    •   FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to monitor, inspect, and review all files, emails, and
        internet use to ensure compliance with this policy.




4. Acceptable Use
Employees, contractors, and any individuals with access to FiftyFive Technologies's information
systems are expected to use these resources in a manner that supports the business objectives of the
organization. The following outlines acceptable use:

    4.1 Business Purposes

        •   Use FiftyFive Technologies's resources, including email, internet, software, and
            hardware, to perform your job responsibilities and tasks effectively.
        •   Access only the information and systems that are necessary for your role and
            responsibilities.
        •   Ensure all communications and data transmissions are conducted in a professional
            manner that aligns with the company’s values and ethical standards.

4.2 Data Protection and Confidentiality

   •   Handle all company data, including customer information, intellectual property, and
       internal communications, with the utmost care and confidentiality.
   •   Ensure that sensitive data is only accessed, shared, or stored in accordance with FiftyFive
       Technologies's data protection policies and applicable regulations.
   •   Report any accidental or unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information to the
       appropriate department immediately.

4.3 Resource Utilization

   •   Use resources efficiently, including bandwidth, storage, and processing power. Avoid
       actions that unnecessarily consume excessive system resources.
   •   Conserve energy by turning off or hibernating systems and devices when not in use,
       particularly overnight or during long periods of inactivity.

4.4 Compliance with Legal and Regulatory Requirements

   •   Ensure that your use of FiftyFive Technologies resources complies with all applicable
       laws, regulations, and contractual obligations.
   •   Familiarize yourself with relevant legal standards, such as copyright laws, data protection
       regulations (e.g., GDPR), and industry-specific requirements (e.g., HIPAA for
       healthcare).

4.5 Training and Awareness

   •   Participate in any mandatory training sessions related to the acceptable use of technology,
       information security, or data protection.
   •   Stay informed about company policies and industry best practices to ensure ongoing
       compliance and security.

4.6 Remote Work and Mobile Device Use

   •   When working remotely, ensure that all company resources are accessed through secure,
       company-approved methods, such as VPNs or other encryption technologies.
   •   Use mobile devices, including smartphones and tablets, in accordance with the
       company’s mobile device management policy, ensuring that they are secured and
       regularly updated.

4.7 Collaboration Tools

   •   Utilize company-approved collaboration tools, such as video conferencing, instant
       messaging, and project management platforms, for work-related communication and
       collaboration.
   •   Ensure that all usage of collaboration tools adheres to company standards for
       professionalism, security, and confidentiality.

5. Unacceptable Use

Unacceptable use of FiftyFive Technologies resources includes, but is not limited to:

    •   Accessing, downloading, or distributing obscene, offensive, or illegal material.
    •   Engaging in activities that could damage, disrupt, or compromise the company’s systems or
        network security.
    •   Using company resources for personal financial gain or political activities.
    •   Sharing confidential or proprietary information without proper authorization.
    •   Installing unauthorized software or hardware on company systems.
    •   Engaging in activities that could result in a conflict of interest with FiftyFive Technologies.




6. Email and Communication Activities

    •   Use company email primarily for business-related communications.
    •   Do not use company email to send spam, chain letters, or unsolicited commercial
        communications.
    •   Be cautious when opening email attachments or links from unknown sources to avoid
        phishing or malware attacks.
    •   Ensure that all communications are respectful and do not harass, discriminate, or defame
        others.




7. Internet Usage

    •   Internet access provided by FiftyFive Technologies should be used primarily for business
        purposes.
    •   Do not visit websites that are known for containing inappropriate or illegal content.
    •   Avoid streaming media for non-work-related purposes, as it can consume significant
        bandwidth.



8. Social Media

    •   Employees must not post confidential or proprietary information about FiftyFive
        Technologies, its clients, or partners on social media.
    •   Personal opinions expressed on social media should not be represented as those of FiftyFive
        Technologies.
    •   Employees must adhere to the company’s social media policy [if available] when using social
        media.

9. Security and Passwords

    •   Employees are responsible for maintaining the security of their account passwords and must
        not share them with others.
    •   Use strong passwords that comply with the company’s password policy.
    •   Report any suspicious activity or potential security breaches to the IT department
        immediately.




10. Consequences of Violations

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of
employment. In some cases, legal action may also be taken.




11. Policy Review

This policy will be reviewed annually and updated as necessary to ensure its continued effectiveness
and relevance.

                                   Assets Policy
                               

This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change any
                                  time as per the company policy.

            Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
           Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)




     2

                                            ASSETS POLICY
1. Provision of Assets
i. Laptop
           Standard configuration of laptops shall be provided to all the employees on the basis of
           following mentioned details:
                       ❖ For any Developer, QA Engineer or any similar IT Based profile
                             Minimum 16 GB RAM (up to 32 GB) and 512 GB SSD Hard Disk with the
                             processor of i5/i7 according to the profile.
                       ❖ For any Sales, HR, Accountant, Designer or any similar non-IT Profile
                             Minimum 16 GB RAM and 512 GB SSD Hard Disk with the processor of i5.




ii. Provision of Laptop Based on Location
   •       For employees working from Jaipur office the laptop can be provided on the date of joining
           itself
   •       For employees joining from Gurgaon and Indore office the laptop will be dispatched after 7
           working days from the date of joining
   •       For employees joining from home the laptop will be dispatched after 21 working days from the
           date of joining




iii. Spare Laptop for Work From Home
   •       For employees joining from home, a spare laptop has to be arranged till the company laptop is
           not received by him/her.
   •       If the spare laptop is not available, the employee needs to inform the asset manager while
           onboarding itself, and the laptop may be collected by the employee as stated in the clause
           below.




       3

iv. Urgent Laptop Requirement
    •       If in case the employee has an urgent need of the laptop and the work quality is getting affected
            due to unavailability of proper laptop, employee will have to collect their laptop from Jaipur
            office after a prior discussion and approval from asset manager and reporting manager.




v. Screen, Mobile, Tablet, Testing Devices
    •       Employee is eligible for the provision of a screen/monitor, Mobile, Tablet & Testing devices for
            the purpose of work if and only if the following conditions are satisfied:
    •       There is client based or project based requirement of the assets. The Request of devices like
            mobile, tablet, testing devices, etc., should be approved by the direct reporting manager of the
            employee
    •       The company will not provide external monitors to employees by default.
    •       An external monitor will be issued only if it is absolutely required for client delivery, mandated
            by a specific project, or approved due to medical necessity.
    •       All requests must include a written justification from the Reporting Manager and require final
            approval from Management and/or the Asset Manager.
    •       Interns, hybrid employees, and remote employees are not eligible for an external monitor.
    •       The screen or monitor cannot be provided or carried to the home/any other destination subject to
            prior approval from reporting manager & Assets manager.


If in case any of the above conditions are not satisfied, the case shall be handled by the asset manager
and the final decision will be taken on the basis of requirement/urgency and location of provision,
subject to prior approval of management.




        4

vi. General Conditions
   •       Provision of asset is subject to availability
   •       Any customized or upgraded asset provision apart from the standard configuration will be
           subject to the approval by management.
   •       The final decision for provision of assets remains with the management




2. Lost or Theft of Assets
   The safety and security of assets provided by the company is the responsibility of an employee. In
   the event of lost or theft of an asset, following actions shall be taken by the employee on immediate
   basis:
           •   The incident shall be reported to Asset Manager and Reporting Manager
           •   A FIR should be filed by the employee and a copy of the FIR should be mailed to Asset
               Manager, keeping Accounts Manager and Reporting Manager in CC


   A committee shall be formed consisting of Asset Manager, Accounts Manager and Reporting
   Manager which would be responsible for investigating, analyzing and reporting the case of loss or
   theft.
           •   The employee shall bear the cost of the loss due to lost or stolen laptop.
           •   The cost would include the depreciated value of asset in the beginning of the current
               financial year and the value of data the asset holds (if any)
           •   The above said committee would be deciding the cost which is to be borne by the
               employee.

           •   Repayment installments can vary if the above said committee agrees on any other
               distribution.




       5

  i. Lost or Stolen and Found Asset
          •   If an asset is lost/stolen and is found at a later stage by the employee, the employee shall
              inform the asset manager on priority basis.
          •   After checking the condition of the asset, the asset manager would then take charge of the
              laptop.
          •   The amount which has been charged for the asset which was lost or stolen shall be refunded
              back to the employee, if the asset is in working state.

          •   If in case there are any damages which are not covered under the brand warranty, the repair
              amount shall be deducted from the refunded amount.



  Please Note: The Final decision in any case if lost or theft stays with the management.




3. Damage
  •       Safety of an asset remains the responsibility of the employee.
  •       If there is any physical damage to an asset, the incident shall immediately be reported to the
          Asset Manager on Keka Help Desk.
  •       The case would be analyzed by the asset manager on first stage, then based on the location of
          the employee, following actions would be taken:
                        ❖ Jaipur Office
                           The employee shall connect with the Asset Manager directly and can proceed
                           accordingly
                        ❖ Gurgaon Office or Work From Home
                           The employee will have to take the asset to nearest official service center of the
                           respective brand and get the asset checked




      6

   Repair Conditions
           ❖ If the damage is not covered under the brand warranty, the employee is liable to bear the
               cost incurred in repair of the asset.
           ❖ Company would be bearing an amount of up to INR 3000 out of the total repair cost which
               is not covered under brand warranty.
           ❖ Employees will only be eligible for the above said amount if the damage is accidental or
               due to unavoidable reasons.
           ❖ Any intentional or careless damage will not be covered.
           ❖ The employee shall ensure repairs are done only at official service centers.
           ❖ Proper invoice must be submitted to asset manager and accounts manager.


   •       If the asset is fully non-functional until repaired, employee should arrange a spare asset or
           collect from Jaipur office.


   •       Spare asset provision is subject to availability.




4. New Asset Requirement / Asset Upgradation
   •       Request must be generated on Keka “Request an Asset” section by the employee.
   •       The request shall be approved by the Reporting Manager followed by the Asset Manager.
   •       Once approved, asset manager will ensure provision or upgradation of asset.
   •       The provision process can vary depending on the location of the employee and availability of
           the asset.




       7

5. Asset Handover
         Assets are to be handed over in following cases:
         Ending the Employment
             •   Employees must return all assets once employment ends.
             •   Full and Final settlement will be on hold until assets are received.


         Work From Home Employees
             •   If in case a courier is executed, any courier charges shall not exceed from 1500, any
                 charges over the above shall be approved by the reporting manager & asset manager.
             •   In case of a laptop, it can be couriered via any trusted courier facility. Company shall
                 reimburse the courier amount to the employee as per the fixed budget.
             •   If any employee working from home has a screen allotted, they will have to visit the
                 Jaipur office and return the screen at Jaipur office only, no courier would be encouraged
                 in case of screen.
             •   The employee should take care of the assets in transit such as packaging and insurance.


         For Jaipur, Indore and Gurgaon Employees
             •   For any asset allotted to an employee working from an office in Jaipur, Indore, or
                 Gurgaon, the asset shall be returned only to the Jaipur Head Office, either in person or
                 via courier, and the courier cost (refundable in FNF) will be reimbursed up to ₹1500,
                 with any higher courier quotation requiring prior approval from the Asset Manager.
             •   If in case an employee fails to return any of the assets after ending of the employment,
                 the full and final settlement of the employee shall be put on hold until the assets are
                 received by the asset manager.
             •   The responsibility of the asset lies with the employee until the asset is not received by
                 the asset manager. If there is any damage/loss to the asset before that, the employee
                 shall be paying for the damages or loss.




     8

6. Intangible Assets
   Any Intangible item of value to the company held by the employee will also be considered as an
   Asset of the company. Intangible assets can include:
           •   Any course/learning material offered by the company or paid/reimbursed by the company
           •   Any data item of the company (images, documents, code etc.)
           •   Company documents (Policies, Procedures, Notices etc.)
           •   Employee Letters (Offer Letters, Increment Letters etc.)
                             ❖ The intangible assets shall not be shared to any external parties or
                                  exchanged within the employees unless and until permitted by the
                                  management or policy
                             ❖ Any customer data available on an employee's workstation shall also be
                                  considered as an intangible asset of the company.
                             ❖ Any employee violating the terms of this clause shall be liable to strict
                                  disciplinary action.




7. Client Assets / Testing Devices
   •       Any Asset provided by a client or any testing device provided to employee shall also be
           considered as an “asset”
   •       The asset policy shall apply to all the client assets and testing devices as per the above-
           mentioned clauses.




       9

8. Monitor Provision Policy
i. Purpose
       The purpose of this policy is to optimize operational and infrastructure costs while ensuring that
       employees have the necessary tools to perform their roles effectively. Accordingly, the
       company will limit the provision of external monitors and approve them only in essential and
       justified cases.


ii. Policy Statement
       The company follows a “No External Monitor by Default” approach. External monitors will be
       provided only when there is a clear business, project, or medical necessity, subject to formal
       approvals.


iii. Scope
       This policy applies to all employees, including full-time employees, interns, and contractual
       staff, across all departments and locations.


iv. Monitor Provision Guidelines
       External monitors are not provided by default to any employee. A monitor may be issued only if
       it is essential for:
                              ▪   Client delivery requirements
                              ▪   Project-specific mandates
                              ▪   Approved medical necessity
             •   All monitor requests must:
                              ▪   Include a written justification from the Reporting Manager
                              ▪   Receive final approval from the HR and/or Asset Manager
                              ▪   Approval is case-specific and does not set a precedent for future
                                  requests.




      10

v. Eligibility Criteria
A request for an external monitor may be considered only under the following circumstances:
                     •   A client or project requirement explicitly mandates dual-screen or extended
                         display usage.
                     •   A documented medical condition requiring a larger display, subject to HR
                         review and management approval.
                     •   Employees who work from the office on a full-time basis and have a clearly
                         established business need.



vi. Non-Eligibility Criteria (Strictly Not Allowed)
External monitors will not be provided to:
    •    Interns
    •    Hybrid or fully remote employees
    •    Employees without a client-specific or project-mandated requirement
    •    Employees requesting monitors solely for convenience or personal productivity preference



9. Policy Compliance
Non-compliance with this policy may result in:
    •    Rejection of asset requests
    •    Recovery of unauthorized assets
    •    Disciplinary action as per company policies



viii. Policy Review
    •    This policy will be reviewed periodically by HR, IT/Asset Management, and Leadership to
         ensure alignment with operational needs and cost-efficiency goals.

Attendance Policy


                               



 This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change at
                                 any time as per the company policy.



             Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
            Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

Introduction
This Attendance Policy establishes clear guidelines to ensure disciplined workforce management and
uninterrupted business operations at FiftyFive Technologies. All employees are required to report to
their designated office location and adhere to prescribed working hours as per their employment
terms. The policy defines expectations regarding daily attendance, punctuality, leave, and absence
management to maintain operational efficiency, accountability, and workplace consistency. Any
deviation from assigned office attendance must be formally approved through defined organizational
processes.




Applicability
This policy is applicable to all employees of FiftyFive Technologies across all office locations,
including Jaipur, Indore, and Gurgaon, as well as employees working under approved Work from
Home arrangements, unless explicitly stated otherwise.



Types of Working Models
The policy defines attendance tracking, working-hour compliance, and reporting mechanisms
across the three working models followed by the Company, as listed below.

    •   Hybrid Work Model
    •   Permanent / Extended Work from Home
    •   Work From Office (WFO – 5 Days a Week)

For detailed attendance and penalisation policy applicable to each of the above working models,
please refer to the respective provisions section of this policy.

Provisions
Standard Working Hours (All Locations): 8 hours

Standard Shift Timings (All Locations) : 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM

Weekly Working Hours: Minimum of 40 working hours per week, excluding lunch breaks

Break Time : 60 minutes (Lunch/Tea/Short Breaks): Break time allotted for lunch, tea, and short
rests; this duration is excluded from total working hours.

Working hours and break time may vary based on project, role, or client requirements. Any deviation
from standard working hours must be approved in advance by the Reporting Manager and HR
Department.

Employees are expected to maintain punctuality, discipline, and professional conduct to ensure
smooth execution of work.



1. Hybrid Attendance Policy:

This policy defines attendance tracking, working-hour compliance, and work-from-home procedures
for employees following a hybrid work model, ensuring transparency, accountability,
and accurate payroll processing.

   a) Attendance Tracking for Hybrid Employees:

       • All hybrid employees must record their attendance through the office biometric system on
           the days they work from the office.

       • Attendance records must reflect a minimum of 8 working hours per day on KEKA.

       • It is mandatory for all employees to use Compliance Tool to track working
           hours, including while working from home (temporary or permanent).

       • Employees must ensure Compliance Tool is active during working hours and accurately
           reflects time spent on work- related tasks.

b) Early Office Exit & Continuation of Work Remotely

  If an employee needs to leave the office before completing 8 working hours, the following
  process must be followed:

      •       Prior approval must be obtained from the Reporting Manager (RM) and HR.
      •       The employee must clock out through the office biometric system before leaving the
              premises.
      •       If the employee continues working after leaving the office, they must remote clock-in
              on KEKA at the time they resume work.
      •       All remote clock-in requests are subject to approval by the Reporting Manager and HR.
      •       Upon completion of work, the employee must remote clock-out on KEKA.
      •       Total working hours for the day will be calculated based on combined logs from office
              biometric attendance and approved remote clock-in records.

  Failure to follow the above process may result in attendance shortfall and payroll impact.



c) Work From Home (Work from Home) Beyond Permitted Limit

    Hybrid employees are permitted to work from home for up to 2 days per week by default.

    If an employee intends to exceed 2 Work from Home days in a week, the following process
    must be followed:

          •    The employee must seek prior approval via email from both the Reporting
               Manager and HR Department .

          •    Upon approval, HR will raise and apply the Work from Home request on
               KEKA on behalf of the employee.

    Once the Work from Home request is approved on KEKA, the employee must:

          •    Log attendance using KEKA as per Work from Home attendance capture scheme
               for the approved Work from Home days.

d) Employee Responsibility & Attendance Accuracy:

    It is the employee’s responsibility to ensure:

        •   Proper clock-in and clock-out on KEKA

       resources by the company. The assets allotted to the employees are their full responsibility
       and the policies followed as mentioned in our employee’s handbook.

3. Data Security:

   Employees must adhere to company policies regarding data security and confidentiality. This
   includes:

       a. Ensuring the security of company-provided devices and data.

       b. Avoiding the use of public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks for work purposes.

       c. Reporting any security incidents or breaches immediately to the IT department.

       d. It is imperative that each employee upholds strict confidentiality and security
          measures to protect sensitive company data from any unauthorized access, breaches,
          or mishandling.

       e. In the event of any data security incident arising from negligence or non-compliance,
          please be aware that FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to take strict
          disciplinary actions, in accordance with our policies and legal obligations.

   Remote work arrangements will not exempt employees from regular performance
   evaluations.

   Performance will be assessed based on agreed-upon objectives, deliverables, and overall
   contribution to the team.

   In our work-from-home policy, it is explicitly stated that dual employment is not permitted.
   Employees are expected to dedicate their full working hours to FiftyFive Technologies and
   are prohibited from engaging in any other form of employment during their contracted hours.
   This policy is in place to maintain focus, ensure productivity, and prevent any potential
   conflicts of interest.

6. Compliance:

   Employees are expected to comply with all local laws and regulations related to remote work
   by following our terms and conditions mentioned below:

      a. Ensuring a Proper Setup:

          •   It is mandatory that employee should have a stable internet connection.

          •   It is mandatory that employee should have a reliable electricity backup (UPS).

          •   Employees have to maintain a dedicated workspace at all times.

          •   While planning the sprint they have to inform in advance of their absence if any

              planned and managed effectively so that the sprints are delivered on time.



      b. Travelling While Working from Home:

          •   Employees have to inform the team and manager transparently and honestly

Attendance Penalization Policy

Objective

The objective of this policy is to define attendance-related penalties applicable to employees for non-
compliance with the company’s attendance and working hours requirements as recorded on KEKA.
This policy ensures consistency, transparency, and timely payroll processing.



Applicability

This policy applies to all employees of the organization, irrespective of role, level, or work
arrangement, unless explicitly stated otherwise.



Provisions:

      Mandatory Attendance Logging

      Every employee is required to mark their daily attendance on the KEKA application.
      Attendance marking is mandatory for all working days, irrespective of the work arrangement
      (office, hybrid, or work from home).

      Failure to log attendance correctly will result in automatic leave deduction by the system.
      Any resulting negative leave balance shall be treated as Loss of Pay (LOP).

Attendance Penalization Rules

The following penalties are system-driven and automatically applied by KEKA based on
attendance and working hours recorded:



         A. Late Arrival / Early Checkout / Short Working Hours

            Any of the following will attract a penalty:

                •    Less than 8 continuous working hours

                •    Late arrival

                •    Early checkout

            Penalty:

                •    After 2 days, KEKA will deduct 0.5-day (Half-Day) Privilege leave.
                •    In the absence of PL balance, Loss of Pay (LOP) will apply



         B. Working Hours Completion

            Less than 95% but more than 50% of required daily working hours

                •    After 2 days, KEKA will deduct 0.5-day (Half-Day) Privilege leave.
                •    In the absence of PL balance, Loss of Pay (LOP) will apply

             Less than 50% of required daily working hours

                 •   After 2 days, KEKA will deduct 1 day Privilege leave.
                 •   In the absence of PL balance, Loss of Pay (LOP) will apply



         C. Missing Punches

            Missing punch-in or punch-out

                •    After 2 days, KEKA will deduct 1 day Privilege leave.

             If PL balance is insufficient

                •    Loss of Pay (LOP) will be applied

             D. No Attendance Logged

                 If no punch-in and punch-out is recorded:

                     •    After 2 days, KEKA will deduct 1 Privilege Leave

                     •    In the absence of PL balance, Loss of Pay (LOP) will apply



Leave Balance Impact

Any negative Privilege Leave balance will automatically result in Loss of Pay. All attendance
deductions are system-driven, final, and non-negotiable once applied.



Finality of Payroll Processing

        •    Payroll processing begins on the 25th of every month

        •    After this date:

                ❖ Attendance penalties are final

                ❖ No reversals or modifications will be made by HR

                ❖ Payroll will be processed strictly based on KEKA attendance data



Employee Responsibility

Employees are solely responsible for:

    •       Accurate and timely attendance marking on KEKA

    •       Completing required working hours

    •       Regularly monitoring attendance records and leave balances



Enforcement

Non-adherence to this policy may result in:

    •       Leave deduction

    •       Loss of Pay (LOP)

    •       Further disciplinary action as per Company policies

Right to Amend Policies

This Employee Handbook is intended to provide general guidance on Company policies and practices.
FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to amend, modify, suspend, or withdraw any policy,
procedure, or benefit described in this handbook at any time, with or without notice, based on
business, operational, or legal requirements.

Business As Usual Secure Practices Policy

                               


This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change at
                                any time as per the company policy.

            Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
           Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

1. Introduction
This document establishes the standard security practices and procedures to be followed by all
employees, contractors, and third-party vendors of FiftyFive Technologies during their day-to-day
activities. The BAU Secure Practices policy aims to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and
availability of the organization's information assets and mitigate the risk of security incidents.


2. Scope

This policy applies to all individuals who have access to FiftyFive Technologies's systems, networks,
applications, and data, regardless of their role or position within the organization. It encompasses
activities conducted on company premises, remote locations, and while using company-issued or
personal devices to access company resources.




3. Roles and Responsibilities

    3.1 Employees

        •   Employees are responsible for adhering to the security practices outlined in this policy
            and reporting any security concerns or incidents to the appropriate authorities.
        •   Employees must undergo security awareness training regularly to stay informed about
            security best practices and emerging threats.
        •   Employees must protect their access credentials (e.g., passwords, authentication tokens)
            and use them only for authorized purposes.

    3.2 Managers and Supervisors

        •   Managers and supervisors are responsible for ensuring that their teams are aware of and
            comply with the BAU Secure Practices policy.

        •   Managers and supervisors must provide support and resources to facilitate compliance
            with security practices, including training and access to security tools.

        •   Managers and supervisors are accountable for addressing any security-related issues or
            violations within their respective teams.

    3.3 Information Security Team

        •   The Information Security Team is responsible for developing, implementing, and
            maintaining the BAU Secure Practices policy.

        •   The Information Security Team must monitor compliance with security practices,
            investigate security incidents, and enforce disciplinary actions for policy violations.

        •   The Information Security Team will review and update the policy as necessary to address
            changes in technology, regulations, or organizational requirements.

4. BAU Secure Practices

   4.1 Access Control

      •   Access to company systems, networks, and data is granted based on job roles and
          responsibilities.

      •   Employees must use strong authentication methods, such as passwords or multi-factor
          authentication, to access company resources.

      •   Employees must not share their access credentials with unauthorized individuals or use
          another person's credentials to access company systems.

   4.2 Data Protection

      •   Employees must handle sensitive and confidential information with care and follow data
          protection guidelines outlined in the organization's data protection policy.

      •   Encryption must be used to protect sensitive data when transmitted over public networks
          or stored on portable devices.

      •   Employees must adhere to data retention and disposal policies to ensure that data is
          retained only as long as necessary and securely disposed of when no longer needed.

   4.3 Device Security

      •   Company-issued devices must be kept up-to-date with the latest security patches and
          antivirus definitions.

      •   Personal devices used to access company resources must meet minimum security
          requirements, including password protection and encryption.

      •   Lost or stolen devices must be reported to IT immediately to mitigate the risk of
          unauthorized access to company data.

   4.4 Email and Communication Security

      •   Employees must exercise caution when opening email attachments or clicking on links in
          emails, especially from unknown or suspicious senders.

      •   Confidential or sensitive information must not be shared via email or other
          communication channels unless encrypted or securely transmitted.

      •   Employees must report any phishing attempts, suspicious emails, or communication
          security incidents to IT or the Information Security Team.

  4.5 Physical Security

      •   Employees must keep work areas secure and ensure that company-issued devices and
          documents are not left unattended in public areas.

      •   Visitors to company premises must be escorted and supervised at all times to prevent
          unauthorized access to sensitive areas.

      •   Access to physical facilities must be controlled through the use of access badges,
          biometric authentication, or other appropriate measures.

  4.6 Security Awareness Training

      •   All employees must undergo regular security awareness training to stay informed about
          the latest security threats, best practices, and organizational policies.

      •   Training sessions should cover topics such as phishing awareness, social engineering,
          password security, and incident response procedures.

  4.7 Incident Reporting and Response

      •   Employees must promptly report any suspected security incidents or breaches to the
          designated IT/security team.

      •   An incident response plan must be in place, outlining procedures for containing,
          mitigating, and recovering from security incidents.

      •   Post-incident reviews should be conducted to identify lessons learned and improve the
          organization's security posture.




5. Compliance

  •   Non-compliance with this policy may result in disciplinary action, including but not limited to
      termination of employment, contract termination, and legal consequences as appropriate.

Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy

                             


This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change at
                                any time as per the company policy.

           Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
          Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

1. Purpose
The purpose of this Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy is to protect FiftyFive Technologies's
sensitive and confidential information from unauthorized access, loss, or theft. This policy sets out
guidelines to ensure that workspaces and computer screens are secure when unattended, promoting a
culture of information security and reducing potential risks associated with information exposure.




2. Scope
This policy applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, temporary and other workers, including
third-party vendors who have access to FiftyFive Technologies's physical or virtual workspaces. It
covers all workspaces and devices where sensitive information is accessed, processed, or stored.




3. Objectives
    •   Protect sensitive and confidential information from unauthorized access or exposure.

    •   Minimize risks related to data loss, theft, or accidental disclosure.

    •   Promote secure working practices for a clean, organized, and secure workspace environment.




4. Definitions
    •   Clear Desk: Practice of keeping desks free of documents and other materials containing
        sensitive or confidential information when they are not in use.

    •   Clear Screen: Practice of locking or logging off computer screens when not in use to prevent
        unauthorized access to displayed information.




5. Roles and Responsibilities
    •   All Employees and Contractors: Comply with clear desk and screen practices, and ensure
        confidential information is protected at all times.

    •   Managers and Supervisors: Ensure team members adhere to this policy and encourage good
        security practices.

    •   IT and Security Team: Provide technical support to enforce clear screen requirements and
        educate users on best practices.

    •   Facilities Management: Provide secure storage options, such as lockable drawers and
        cabinets, for sensitive information.

6. Policy Statements
   6.1 Clear Desk Requirements

      •   Document Security: All sensitive and confidential documents must be securely stored in
          lockable cabinets, drawers, or designated storage areas when not actively in use.

      •   End-of-Day Desk Clearing: Employees must clear all sensitive information and
          materials from their desks at the end of each workday. This includes removing any
          documents, notes, removable storage devices, and equipment that contain or access
          sensitive information.

      •   Temporary Absence Protocol: If an employee is away from their desk for extended
          periods during the day, they must ensure that all sensitive materials are secured in a
          locked drawer or file cabinet.

      •   Secure Printing: Employees must retrieve printed documents immediately and avoid
          leaving them unattended on printers or shared desks. If printed materials are sensitive,
          employees should use secure printing options, such as requiring a code to release the
          document.

   6.2 Clear Screen Requirements

      •   Screen Locking Standards: All employees must lock their computer screens whenever
          stepping away from their workstation, regardless of the duration. This can be done by
          using keyboard shortcuts (e.g., "Ctrl + Alt + Del" or "Windows Key + L" on Windows or
          enabling screen saver lock on Mac).

      •   Automatic Screen Lock Configuration: IT will configure all devices to automatically
          lock screens after a set period of inactivity (e.g., 5–15 minutes), based on organizational
          risk tolerance and regulatory requirements.

      •   Use of Privacy Screens: Employees handling sensitive information in open or public
          workspaces must use privacy screens on monitors to prevent unauthorized viewing of
          displayed information.

      •   Remote Work Screen Security: When working remotely, employees must follow the
          same clear screen practices and ensure that screen visibility is limited to authorized
          individuals only.

   6.3 Physical Security of Devices and Media

      •   Securing Laptops and Mobile Devices: Employees must lock or secure laptops, mobile
          devices, and other equipment when not in use, especially in shared or open environments.
          This includes using physical locks when available.

      •   Storage of Removable Media: USB drives, external hard drives, and other removable
          media should be securely stored when not in use and must not be left unattended on desks
          or in shared areas.

      •   Confidential Document Disposal: Sensitive and confidential information must be
          disposed of in secure shred bins, not left in general recycling or trash bins.

    6.4 Shared and Open Workspaces

        •   Clean Desk in Shared Spaces: Employees using shared desks or workstations must clear
            all documents, notes, and electronic devices before leaving to maintain a clutter-free and
            secure workspace.

        •   Meeting Room Practices: Employees must remove all materials containing sensitive
            information, erase any information from whiteboards, and ensure that no confidential
            documents are left behind in meeting rooms.

        •   Secure Document Removal: Any confidential information brought into shared or open
            workspaces must be removed or securely stored after use.

    6.5 Confidential Information Handling

        •   Labeling and Storing Sensitive Information: Documents and materials containing
            confidential information should be appropriately labelled and handled according to data
            classification policies. Such information must be securely stored when not in use.

        •   Privacy Practices: Employees must position screens and documents to limit the exposure
            of sensitive information to unauthorized individuals, particularly in areas with public or
            open access.

    6.6 Monitoring and Compliance

        •   Periodic Compliance Checks: Supervisors, managers, and the Information Security
            team may conduct random spot checks and periodic reviews to ensure compliance with
            this policy.

        •   Employee Awareness and Training: Employees will receive regular reminders and
            training sessions to reinforce clear desk and screen practices and to ensure understanding
            of data protection responsibilities.

        •   Incident Reporting: Employees are required to report any policy violations, security
            incidents, or observations of non-compliance to their supervisors or the Information
            Security team promptly.

7. Compliance
Non-compliance with this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination, as
per FiftyFive Technologies's Code of Conduct. Employees and contractors are expected to follow this
policy strictly to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive information.

8. Exceptions
Any exception to this policy must be approved in writing by the Information Security Officer or
designated authority, with documentation explaining the reason and duration of the exception.

9. Review and Updates

This policy will be reviewed annually or whenever there are significant changes in
operational practices or security requirements. Any revisions will be communicated to all
employees and stakeholders.

                      Code of Ethics & Business Conduct
                              

This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change any
                                  time as per the company policy.



            Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
           Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)




2

For all employees, the following guidelines/code of conduct are applicable:

CODE OF ETHICS & BUSINESS CONDUCT

Statement
This Code of Ethics & Business Conduct (CEBC) applies to all employees working at FiftyFive
Technologies, its subsidiaries, and joint ventures over which FiftyFive Technologies exercises
management control ("We", "Us. Our. "Company").

Our Code has been created to help support employees working with the Company. This code is to
maintain and reinforce required standards of behaviors for the effective working of our company to
provide an inclusive environment to all our employees and is a step in the direction of protecting the
interests of all stakeholders.

Objective
To provide a performing, inclusive, safe, and growth-oriented environment for all employees in
FiftyFive Technologies through this CEBC. This policy states the expected behaviors of every
employee while and during employment with the company.

Scope
The behaviors at the workplace are critical in delivering the desired results in all our roles impacting
our performance and growth, hence, it is critical for every employee to follow this code very
meticulously. The violation of the code may call for investigation, warning, censure, transfers
(departments, location, or roles), demotions, holding of salaries and benefits, and in serious violations
including termination of employment.

Definitions
Employees: Full-time employees, Interns, Trainees, Consultants (Full and part-time), and contractors.
Behaviors: Actions taken at the workplace during the time of employment with the company
including all commissions and omissions.

Workplace: All offices, remote workplaces, client locations, online environments, such as the
Internet, and any other place where any official work/meeting is being conducted.

Code of Ethics & Business Conduct: Guidelines for behaviors during employment with FiftyFive
Technologies.

Conflict of Interest: A “conflict of interest occurs when an employee’s activities, transactions,
interests, influences and/or relationships, both inside and outside of the company interfere in anyway
with the employee’s performance of their job duties or the interests of the Company as a whole.




3

1. Employee Data Privacy

    •   The Company is committed to protecting the privacy and confidentiality of employee
        personal data. Employee information is collected, processed, and stored only for legitimate
        business, employment, legal, and compliance purposes. These purposes may include
        recruitment, onboarding, payroll, benefits administration, performance management, IT and
        information security, and statutory or regulatory reporting.

    •   Access to employee data is strictly restricted to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis.
        The Company implements appropriate technical, administrative, and organizational
        safeguards to prevent unauthorized access, misuse, loss, or disclosure of employee
        information.

    •   Employee data may be shared with third parties only where required by applicable law,
        contractual obligations, or legitimate business necessity. Such data shall be retained only for
        as long as necessary to fulfill its intended purpose or to comply with legal requirements.

    •   Employees are expected to safeguard personal and Company data at all times and must
        promptly report any suspected or actual data breach, unauthorized access, or misuse to the HR
        Department immediately. Accessing another employee’s personal information through
        Company platforms or portals without the consent of the concerned employee or without
        official authorization is strictly discouraged and may lead to disciplinary action.




4

2. Conflict of Interest
A “conflict of interest occurs when an employee’s actions, transactions, interests, and/or relationships,
both inside and outside of the company interfere in any way with the employee/team/company’s
interests and work.

The following are some examples of conflict-of-interest situations:

Any activity that may oblige one to an outside entity such as a supplier or a customer.

    ● Holding a financial interest in a competitor or vendor company of FiftyFive Technologies
       where one could personally affect the business with that company. Financial interest could
       include, ownership of capital stock, bonds, or notes; partnership interest; direct or indirect
       interest through a family member, trust or other relationship.

    ● Working on a part-time, temporary basis, moonlighting, freelancing, or providing advisory
       consultancy to another organization/person/business.

    ● Any activity carried out with the support of or through family or friends for mis-utilizing the
       company resources, facilities, and equipment.

    ● Receiving disproportionate/special gifts, discounts, and benefits, which are not generally
       offered by an outside concern while being in a position to influence the company decisions.

    ● Working with any not-for-profit entity where you can influence the company's investment
       decisions.

    ● Preferential hiring, promoting, supervising, directing business to, investing in, or in any other
       manner favoring a family member or friend, without the prior written consent from the
       management.

       Note: On occurrence/potential occurrence of such conflict, the Employee shall disclose such
       information to their supervisor/manager over mail; Try and avoid entering such a transaction
       without the guidance of the supervisor/manager. The appropriate parties will decide to
       determine if the conflict is substantial enough to exclude the Employee from any further
       involvement in such activity or decision process.




5

3. Maintaining Accurate Records
    The employees are mandatorily required to keep accurate, complete information in a timely
    manner to:

     ● Meet our legal obligations.

     ● Ensure any reports that are based on those records are also accurate and complete. The records
        include all work-related documents, emails, spreadsheets, notes, reports (including timecard
        records and operating metrics), financial records, plans, procedures, and process documents,
        business information, including engagement documents and deliverables, payroll records,
        performance evaluations, and time and expense reports.

     Note: The security of these documents is also the responsibility of the concerned employee.



4. Protecting Customer Data
    Leaking, manipulating, mismanagement, stealing or mishandling of any customer data, be it
    confidential or otherwise is strictly prohibited. Employees deployed on projects are trusted with
    sensitive information considering that they have understood all the clauses of the Non-Disclosure
    Agreement (NDA).

    The NDA restricts the employee to:

       ● Share/disclose client information whether during or after their employment with FiftyFive
          Technologies.

       ● Use the information for any kind of benefit (personal or otherwise) or engage with an entity
          relating to the employer’s business, during their employment and till 12 months of their
          separation from the company.

       ● Publishing the customer data, code, or any other documents of the company on platforms
          such as GitHub is not only prohibited but also illegal.




6

5. Protecting Intellectual Property Rights
    The intellectual property of FiftyFive Technologies is a strategic and valuable asset and must be
    adequately protected. Intellectual property includes, but is not limited to, patents, copyrights,
    trademarks, trade secrets, inventions, software source code, designs, documents, methodologies,
    data, and all work products created during the course of employment.

    Employees are expected to take all necessary steps to protect the Company’s proprietary and
    confidential information and to respect the intellectual property rights of others. In certain
    circumstances, employees may be required to share confidential information with third parties
    such as customers, vendors, or suppliers. Any such disclosure must be made with utmost care and
    strictly in accordance with the Company’s policies, approvals, and processes.

    Unauthorized use, copying, distribution, or disclosure of intellectual property—including software,
    proprietary tools, or training materials—is strictly prohibited and may be illegal.

    Confidentiality and intellectual property obligations continue even after the termination of
    employment. Any violation may result in disciplinary action, including termination, and may also
    lead to legal consequences.



6. Anti-Money Laundering
    Definition of Money Laundering

    Money laundering refers to any process used to disguise the origin of illegally obtained money to
    make it appear legitimate. This includes, but is not limited to:

         •   Concealing the source of funds

         •   Converting illegal money into legal assets

         •   Using Company resources or systems for unlawful financial transactions



    Employee Responsibilities

    All employees are required to:

        •    Act with integrity and honesty in all financial and business dealings

        •    Ensure that Company funds, reimbursements, and transactions are used only for
             legitimate business purposes

        •    Follow all internal financial controls, approval processes, and documentation
             requirements

        •    Complete any mandatory AML or compliance training provided by the Company
7

    Prohibited Activities

    Employees must not:

        •    Engage in or facilitate money laundering or financial fraud

        •    Accept or process funds that are suspected to be from illegal sources

        •    Create false invoices, expense claims, or financial records

        •    Circumvent financial controls or approval mechanisms

        •    Assist any individual or entity in hiding or misrepresenting the source of funds


    Identification and Reporting of Suspicious Activities

    Employees must immediately report any suspicious activity, including but not limited to:

        •   Unusual or unexplained financial transactions

        •   Requests to process payments without proper documentation

        •   Pressure to bypass standard approval or compliance procedures

        •   Any activity that appears inconsistent with the employee’s role or Company operations

            Reports should be made confidentially to:

        •   The HR Department, or

        •   The Finance / Compliance Team, or

        •   The Reporting Manager

    The Company ensures that no employee will face retaliation for reporting concerns in good faith.


    Record Keeping

    All financial records, invoices, receipts, and approvals must be:

        • Accurate and complete

        • Maintained as per Company policy and applicable laws

        • Available for audit, inspection, or review when required




8

    Compliance with Laws

    The Company complies with all applicable anti-money laundering laws and regulations.
    Employees are expected to adhere to all relevant legal and regulatory requirements at all times.



    Disciplinary Action

    Any violation of this policy may result in:

         • Disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment

         • Legal action, where applicable

         • Reporting to regulatory or law enforcement authorities, if required




7. Anti-Bribery and Corruption
    FiftyFive Technologies is committed to conducting all its business activities with the highest
    standards of ethics, integrity, and transparency and follows a strict zero-tolerance approach toward
    bribery and corruption. Employees must not, directly or indirectly, offer, promise, give, request, or
    accept any bribe, kickback, improper payment, gift, favor, discount, or other undue advantage that
    could influence, or appear to influence, any business decision or relationship. All employees are
    expected to act honestly, professionally, and fairly in all dealings, comply fully with this policy and
    any related training or guidelines, and avoid situations that may create conflicts of interest.

    Any suspected or actual instance of bribery or corrupt practice must be reported immediately to
    HR or Management and will be addressed confidentially and without retaliation. Any violation of
    this policy may result in disciplinary action, including termination of employment, and may also
    attract civil or criminal liability under applicable laws.

    Employee Responsibilities

 a. As an employee of FiftyFive Technologies, you must ensure that you read, understand, and
    comply with the information contained within this policy, and with any training or other anti-
    bribery and corruption information you are given.
 b. All employees and those under our control are equally responsible for the prevention, detection,
    and reporting of bribery and other forms of corruption. They are required to avoid any activities
    that could lead to, or imply, a breach of this anti-bribery policy.
 c. If you have reason to believe or suspect that an instance of bribery or corruption has occurred or
    will occur in the future that breaches this policy, you must notify the compliance manager.
 d. If any employee breaches this policy, they will face disciplinary action and could face dismissal
    for gross misconduct. FiftyFive Technologies has the right to terminate a contractual relationship
    with an employee if they breach this anti-bribery policy.

9

8. Criminal Records Check
     An employee shall, at the employer’s request and cost, submit/agree to a criminal record check.
     The employer may terminate an employee should the criminal record check reveal any
     conviction(s). Additionally, there should not be any pending/running investigation(s) or activities
     registered that might malign the brand image of the company.

        For instance,

     ● The employee should not have been convicted of any felony.

     ● The employee should not have been terminated from employment by any employer or
        contractor for theft, misappropriation of property, or any other potentially illegal or unethical
        acts.

     ● The employee must not have any cases of POSH, disciplinary action(s), or Breach of Code of
        Conduct against them.



9. Performance Standards
      Every employee is expected to meet the performance standards communicated by their reporting
      manager or supervisor, whether verbally or in writing. Employees are expected to:

          •   Meet role-specific goals and responsibilities

          •   Follow Company policies, processes, and ethical guidelines

          •   Demonstrate continuous learning and skill development

          •   Adapt to changing technologies and business requirements

      Additionally, employees must:

          •   Attend training programs as scheduled

          •   Maintain punctuality, discipline, and professional conduct throughout their tenure

          •   Meet assigned deadlines

          •   Maintain quality, accuracy, and consistency in their work




10

10. Etiquette In Meetings
     Employees of FiftyFive Technologies are expected to maintain professionalism and courtesy
     while attending internal or external meetings, regardless of whether the meeting is conducted
     physically or virtually.

     Employees must:

        • Be well-prepared for meetings and contribute meaningful inputs

        • Ensure necessary arrangements such as internet connectivity, devices, battery backup, and
           required materials are in place

     For virtual meetings, employees are required to:

        • Join from a quiet and distraction-free location

        • Keep cameras on unless otherwise instructed

        • Mute microphones when not speaking

        • Use professional and respectful language at all times

     Employees should take notes during meetings, assist in preparing Minutes of Meeting (MoMs)
     where required, and adhere to agreed action points. All participants are expected to conduct
     themselves professionally, with dignity, respect, and courtesy toward others at all times.



11. Maintaining Discipline
     An employee shall be subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination of their
     services, for the commission of any of the following offenses, including but not limited to the
     below:

      ●    Excessive absenteeism or tardiness.

      ●    Inattentiveness to work, including but not limited to, failure to start work at the designated
           time, quitting work before proper time, or leaving assigned work area, building, or project
           during working hours without authorization from appropriate supervisor.

      ●    Not filling or falsifying the data filled in the timesheet(s).

      ●    Violation of a safety rule or safety practice.

      ●    Smoking in prohibited areas.

      ●    Vending, soliciting, or collecting contributions in the company's name, time or premises.

      ●    Gambling, lottery, or any other game of chance on the employer's premises during working
           hours.
11
      ●    Any other offense of equal magnitude to the above.

12. Remote Work Etiquette
     Employees must be equally accountable and responsible when they are working remotely, as they
     would be otherwise. The following must be considered while working in an online mode:

      ●    Be punctual for meetings, and be presentable while attending the same, Ensure proper
           connectivity for a smooth flow of work.

      ●    During office hours, even when working remotely, one must be as presentable and dressed
           as if attending a physical office. The same dress code applies to remote working in office.
           Camera must be switched during the meetings just like a face-to-face meeting.

      ●    Not record/share screen for meetings to be outsourced to any unauthorized employee or to
           a third party.

      ●    Not attend client meetings in front of a third party, even if it is a family member.

      ●    Not be under the influence of any intoxicated object during working hours.

      ●    Being unavailable without prior information to the manager even for a short period of time
           is not acceptable.



13. Dress Code
     We are a professional organization and expect a similar demeanor from all the employees. Hence,
     the following must be kept in mind:

      ●    Employees are expected to dress in [business casual, smart casual, business formals attire.

      ●    The attire for men includes formal shirts, t-shirts, formal trousers, jeans, tie, shoes and
           jacket.

      ●    Women's wear consists of jeans, pants, tops, formal skirts and formal shirts, sarees,
           leggings with kurta or kurtis.

      ●    Employees are allowed to wear only decent accessories.

      ●    Employees must always present a clean, professional appearance, even if the meeting is on
           Online Mode.

      ●    Everyone is expected to be well-groomed and wear clean attire, free of holes, tears, or
           other signs of wear and tear.

      ●    Attire with offensive or inappropriate designs or stamps are not allowed and should not be
           too revealing.

      ●    While on a visit to the customers – employees are expected to be formally dressed and
12         well groomed.

     Note:

      1.     Managers or supervisors are expected to inform employees when they are violating the
             dress code.

      2.     Employees in violation are expected to immediately correct the issue. The employee or the
             person who is not in the proper dress code can be asked to change their attire and report to
             HR.

      3.     Repeated violations or violations that have major repercussions may result in disciplinary
             action being taken up to and including termination.



14. Compliance with Laws
     All the employees acting or working on behalf of FiftyFive Technologies are expected to comply
     with all Company's policies, procedures, and regulations with letter and spirit and follow the
     legal requirements of all locations where we do business.

     Violation of applicable state laws, rules, and regulations may subject us to individual criminal or
     civil liability. Such individual violations may also subject the Company to civil or criminal
     liability, to the loss of reputation or business, and both these events may attract disciplinary
     action by the Company.



15. Substance Abuse/ Intoxication
     The Company is committed to providing a safe and productive workplace for its employees.
     While on duty at FiftyFive Technologies, employees are prohibited from:

        ● Selling, possessing, using, and/or distributing drugs, including inhalants, illegal drugs, and
             over-the- counter intoxicating drugs.

        ● Selling, possessing, using, and/or distributing alcoholic
             beverages/weed/marijuana/cannabis.

        ● Driving FiftyFive Technologies vehicles or personal vehicles (if applicable) while under
             the influence of drugs and/or alcohol.

        ● Using and/or distributing prescription drugs that cause drowsiness or impaired
             performance while working or during employment.

        ● Use of tobacco products anywhere on the Company’s premises except in authorized and
             designated locations. The designated smoking areas are Specifically Mentioned (Smoking
             Zone).

13

16. Gifts and Entertainment
      Receiving and giving gifts to any person as a quid pro quo for favors received or provided is not
      acceptable. Gifts such cash and non-cash items, some examples of which are artwork, watches,
      jewelry, equipment, home appliances, services, prizes, gift vouchers, donations to charities, use
      of vacation facilities, stocks or other securities, home improvements, tickets/invitation to sports,
      cultural or any other event is prohibited.

      This does not include reasonable expenditure incurred on account of routine business courtesies
      offered to or received by any business partner as a customary trade practice (e.g., providing
      transportation, meals, accommodation, etc.) during official visits. All the people covered under
      this code need to comply with Anti- bribery and Anti-Corruption laws, or any other applicable
      laws.



17. Blow the Whistle
      Employees are empowered and guided to raise their voices against any misconduct, illegal,
      unethical, or immoral activity.

      Our aim is to:

         ●    Make employees vigilant about wrongdoings; and responsible by giving them the
              appropriate authority.

         ●    Reduce corruption as well as risk.

         ●    Protect employees from retaliation, by keeping their identities confidential.



18. No Retaliation
     FiftyFive Technologies does not support or encourage retaliation. We consider any act of
     retaliation to be misconduct. Retaliation can take many forms, for example: threats, exclusion,
     intimidation, humiliation, exclusion, and raising issues maliciously or in bad faith. All the
     mentioned acts will be subjected to disciplinary action.



19. No Harassment:
     Providing a safe working environment is mandatory for the effective working of every individual,
     no employees feel unsafe at any time of the day and in any environment be it online or offline. Any
     sexual harassment of any employee (all genders included) is considered of a serious nature. Please
     refer to the POSH policy.

14

20. Conduct on social media
     Employees need to be extremely careful while posting any unauthorized content on social media,
     it is not acceptable and will call for investigation and actions by the company. During
     employment, it is mandatory for all employees to be personally responsible for any posts by them
     on social platforms such as YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, WhatsApp, X, and others.
     Any official content posting needs to be approved by the internal marketing team/s.

     The following behaviors by employees on social media are prohibited:

         ● Derogatory comments on any of the social media platforms.

         ● Bad-mouthing the employees/organizations.

         ● Posting illicit/obscene/offensive/biased content related to the organization or otherwise.



21. General Work Practices
     We, as an employer, strongly believe in fostering high performance and inter- team dependency,
     among our employees. For the same reason, we strongly discourage:

         ● Taking credit for the work done by someone else, and not giving them the due
            appreciation for the same.

         ● Getting involved in rumors and gossip mongering, to unnecessarily create an
            environment of insecurity.

         ● Stopping someone from doing authorized work, via undue use of
            position/designation/experience.

         ● Discrimination of all forms but not limited to direct discrimination, Indirect
            discrimination, Harassment,

         ● Victimization, Disability Discrimination, Religious Discrimination, and Discrimination
            on the basis of Race, Color, and Sex.

         ● Bullying in all forms including but not limited to Physical bullying, Verbal bullying,
            social bullying, and Cyberbullying. 26.6.Usage of social media at Workspace including
            but not limited to Instagram, Facebook, Snapchat.

         ● Damage to company property including but not limited to Hardware and Software
            Peripherals And Devices, Company Furniture, and Fixtures.




15

22. Place of Posting & Assignment
     The place of posting of all the employees will be at Jaipur, Indore and Gurgaon or work from
     home. However, an employee can be sent to other countries or other parts of India for training,
     work, or some other assignment that is project-related.



23. Whole Time Service
     During the period of employment with FiftyFive Technologies, employees are required to devote
     their full working time, attention, and abilities exclusively to the Company. Employees shall not,
     directly or indirectly, engage in any other employment, business, profession, consultancy,
     freelance work, or commercial activity—whether paid or unpaid—without obtaining prior
     written approval from the Company’s Management. Under no circumstances shall an employee
     engage in any activity that conflicts with the Company’s interests or affects job performance.
     Any violation of this policy may result in disciplinary action, including immediate termination of
     employment, and may also lead to legal action as deemed appropriate by the Company.



24. Right to Amend Policies

     This Employee Handbook is intended to provide general guidance on Company policies and
     practices. FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to amend, modify, suspend, or withdraw any
     policy, procedure, or benefit described in this handbook at any time, with or without notice,
     based on business, operational, or legal requirements.




16
