Continual Improvement Policy


                              


This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change at
                                any time as per the company policy.


            Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
           Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

1. Purpose
The purpose of this Continual Improvement Policy is to define the framework and principles for
continuously enhancing the quality and effectiveness of FiftyFive Technologies's products, services,
and processes. This policy aims to foster a culture of improvement and innovation throughout the
organization.




2. Scope
This policy applies to all employees, departments, and functions within FiftyFive Technologies. It
encompasses all aspects of operations, including product development, service delivery, and process
management.




3. Definitions
    •   Continual Improvement: An ongoing effort to enhance products, services, and processes to
        achieve better performance, efficiency, and effectiveness.

    •   Improvement Opportunity: A chance to enhance or optimize processes, products, or
        services based on feedback, performance data, or changing requirements.




4. Policy Statement
FiftyFive Technologies is committed to the continual improvement of its operations, products, and
services. We strive to exceed customer expectations, improve performance, and adapt to changes in
the industry and market conditions. All employees are encouraged to contribute to the improvement
process by identifying opportunities and implementing solutions.

5. Principles of Continual Improvement
   •   Customer Focus: Understand and meet customer needs and expectations. Use customer
       feedback to drive improvements.

   •   Data-Driven Decision Making: Use data and performance metrics to identify areas for
       improvement and measure the effectiveness of improvement actions.

   •   Employee Involvement: Engage employees at all levels in the improvement process.
       Encourage and recognize their contributions and ideas.

   •   Process Approach: Focus on improving processes to achieve better results. Identify and
       eliminate inefficiencies and bottlenecks.

   •   Leadership Commitment: Demonstrate leadership and support for continual improvement
       initiatives. Allocate resources and provide guidance to ensure success.

   •   Innovation: Foster a culture of innovation by encouraging creative thinking and exploring
       new approaches to problem-solving.



6. Continual Improvement Process
   6.1 Identification of Improvement Opportunities

       •   Feedback: Gather feedback from customers, employees, and other stakeholders to
           identify areas for improvement.

       •   Data Analysis: Analyze performance data, audit results, and other metrics to pinpoint
           inefficiencies or opportunities for enhancement.

       •   Benchmarking: Compare performance against industry standards and best practices to
           identify gaps and improvement areas.

   6.2 Planning and Implementation

       •   Action Plan: Develop a plan to address identified improvement opportunities. Include
           specific actions, responsible individuals, and timelines.

       •   Resource Allocation: Allocate necessary resources, including time, budget, and
           personnel, to implement improvement initiatives.

       •   Execution: Implement the action plan, ensuring that all tasks are completed as planned
           and in accordance with established procedures.

   6.3 Monitoring and Evaluation

      •   Tracking: Monitor the progress of improvement initiatives and track key performance
          indicators (KPIs) to assess effectiveness.

      •   Evaluation: Evaluate the results of improvement actions to determine their impact on
          performance, efficiency, and customer satisfaction.

      •   Adjustment: Make adjustments as needed based on evaluation results to ensure ongoing
          effectiveness and continuous improvement.

   6.4 Communication and Training

      •   Communication: Communicate improvement goals, plans, and results to all employees
          and relevant stakeholders.

      •   Training: Provide training and support to employees to ensure they understand and can
          effectively contribute to improvement efforts.

   6.5 Review and Feedback

      •   Review: Conduct regular reviews of the continual improvement process to assess its
          effectiveness and identify areas for further enhancement.

      •   Feedback: Collect feedback from employees and stakeholders on the improvement
          process and use it to refine and improve the policy.




7. Roles and Responsibilities
   7.1 Leadership Team

      •   Support: Provide leadership and support for continual improvement initiatives. Ensure
          alignment with organizational goals and objectives.

      •   Resource Allocation: Allocate resources and provide guidance to facilitate the
          implementation of improvement actions.

   7.2 Department Managers

      •   Implementation: Ensure that improvement initiatives are implemented within their
          departments and that employees are engaged in the process.

      •   Monitoring: Monitor departmental performance and identify opportunities for
          improvement.

    7.3 Employees

        •   Participation: Actively participate in improvement activities, provide feedback, and
            suggest ideas for enhancing processes and performance.

        •   Compliance: Follow established procedures and contribute to the successful
            implementation of improvement initiatives.



8. Policy Compliance and Enforcement
    8.1 Compliance

        •   Regulatory Requirements: Ensure that improvement activities comply with applicable
            laws, regulations, and industry standards.

        •   Internal Audits: Conduct regular audits to assess compliance with this policy and
            identify areas for improvement.

    8.2 Enforcement

        •   Disciplinary Actions: Non-compliance with this policy may result in disciplinary
            actions. Ensure that enforcement measures are consistent with company policies and legal
            requirements.



9. Policy Review and Updates

This policy will be reviewed annually or as needed to ensure it remains relevant and effective.
Updates will be communicated to all employees and relevant stakeholders.

Leave Policy
                             



This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change any
                                  time as per the company policy.



            Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
           Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

Introduction
This leave policy outlines the guidelines governing the leave entitlements, accrual and usage for
employees of the organisation. The policy is designed to ensure fair and consistent application of
leave benefits, support employee well-being and enable effective workforce and project planning
while meeting statutory and operational requirements.



Type of Leaves
As per company’s leave policy, leave types are categorised into two main categories:

    a) Monthly Leaves
    b) Additional Leaves

Each comprising of specific sub-categories as defined under the respective leave provisions.

Leave Provisions

Monthly Leaves

Leaves are provided on a monthly pro-rata basis and are accrued at the beginning of each
month. Employees are entitled to a total of 24 leaves per year, comprising Casual Leave
(CL) and Privilege Leave (PL). Employees are expected to plan and apply for their leaves in advance
through the HRIS Leave Management System to enable effective project and resource planning.



1. Casual Leave:

Purpose

The purpose of the Casual Leave Policy is to enable employees to plan short-term time off from
work for personal and unforeseen requirements. Casual Leave may be availed for reasons such as rest
and de-stressing, personal commitments, appearing for examinations, family events (including
marriage of family members), minor illness, or other personal exigencies.



Eligibility

This Policy is applicable to:

    •   All Full-time employees of FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited including support
        staff, trainees and probationers.

This policy is not applicable to:

    •     Business Associates, Associate Consultant / Contractual Employee, Freelancers

Provisions

a) Entitlement:

    •   The employees are entitled to 12 working days of Casual leave every year.

    •   The year for the purpose of leave accounting is the year from January to December.

    •   These types of leaves are a part of the total of 24 leaves allowed to an employee in a year
        that can be taken for some casual work.

    •   The casual leave will be credited on a pro rata monthly basis, i.e. 1 in a month.

    •   The leave entitlement for the year is prorated every month to arrive at the monthly
        entitlement.

    •   The entitlement for each month is credited at the beginning of each month.

    •    All Unutilized Causal leaves lapse at the end of the calendar year and cannot be
        reimbursed through any monetary means.



b) Availing the benefits:

    •   The leave may be prefixed and or suffixed with other leave types/weekends/statutory
        holidays. Intervening weekends and holidays are not counted as Casual Leave days
        and cannot be combined with Paternity Leave, Maternity Leave, Adoption Leave, Exam
        Leave.

    •   These leaves can only be combined with Privilege leave; Floater Leave and Bereavement
        Leave.

    •   Leaves may be applied for a minimum of half a day.

    •   Employees may apply for leave multiple times during the year, subject to availability of the
        balance. However, such applicants must not violate the principle and purpose for which casual
        leave is provided.

    •   Leave when availed more than 2 days needs to be informed well in advance before a prior
        notice of 7 days.

    •   The leave days in a request may span across the years.

    •   The leaves cannot be applied after availing the same, hence no back-date leaves can be
        applied. If not, the applied prior may use his/her discretion to convert this into a Loss of
        pay.

    •   If the employee applies for Casual Leave but does not avail of the same due to any reason,
        he/she may choose to cancel the same.

c) Special Scenarios

   •   New Joined:

       The employee can avail leave if he/she has sufficient balance.

       Casual Leave for employees who join during the year will be credited after their first
       payroll run and their entitlement will be prorated based on their joining.

   •   Employee goes on leave without pay (LWP):

       The employee is not entitled to leave when he/she is on leave without pay, hence there will be
       no leave of credit for the duration of the LWP.

   •   Employee serving notice period:

       The employee serving period cannot avail of Casual leave at the time they have started
       serving the notice period.

   •   Employee in Performance Improvement Plan (PIP):

       The employee in PIP cannot avail of Casual leave at this time.



Terms and Conditions

   •   You are not allowed to apply past day leave. Your manager or HR manager can apply on your
       behalf.

   •   Casual Leave requires comment while applying for leave.

   •   Casual Leave cannot be applied when in the notice period and during the performance
       improvement plan.

   •   Casual Leave cannot be taken along with Paternity Leave, Maternity Leave, Exam Leave,
       Adoption Leave.

   •   In case the leave is rejected after it is availed, and the employee is still on leave, it will be
       considered a loss of pay and the employee will be subject to disciplinary actions based on
       HR’s discretion.

   •   During the leave period, the employee cannot take up any part-time or full-time employment
       of remuneration or otherwise, for any reason whatsoever.

Procedure

Applying for Leave:

        o     The employee can apply for leave through the Keka Portal.

        o     Login to KEKA-Go to Me section- Click on Leave- Apply for Leave.

        o     The employee completed the leave application form and submitted it for approval of the
              same.

              Note: The employee can also view the details of previous leaves availed and outstanding
              balance through the KEKA app.

Approval Workflow:

        o     The leave goes for two levels of approval: to the employee's immediate Reporting
              Manager and to the Branch Head.



2. Privileged Leave (PL)

Purpose

This Policy is designed to enable employees to plan their time off from work. The purpose of
the privilege leave policy is to grant the employee a fixed number of days off from work. As
a benefit they have earned on account of working for a specific number of days in a particular period.



Eligibility

This Policy is applicable to:

    •   All Full-time employees of FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited including trainees and
        probationers.

This policy is not applicable to:

    •     Support Staff, Business Associates, Associate Consultant / Contractual Employee,
          Freelancers

Provisions

a) Entitlement:

   •   The employees are entitled to 12 working days of Privilege Leaves every year.

   •   The year for the purpose of leave accounting is the year from January to December.

   •   These types of leaves are a part of the total of 24 leaves allowed to an employee in a year.

   •   The leave of entitlement for the year is prorated on a monthly basis to arrive at the monthly
       entitlement. The entitlement for each month is credited at the beginning of each month.

   •   Employees can avail the leave balance of upcoming months in advance based on the
       accumulated balance of projection.

   •   Leaves that are entitled to be carried forward will be up to the days as maximum of 12 in
       a year.

   •   The encashment is processed in the financial year, i.e. March month.

   •   The maximum accumulation of privilege leave balances is capped at a maximum of 24
       days. Number of days left in excess of 24, accumulated till the end of the calendar
       year are treated as “Surplus” in the month of December.

   •   Any excess beyond 24 days will be subject to encashment, and employees
       will be required to either avail of those leaves or the surplus balance into encashment.

b) Availing the benefits:

   •   Employees may apply for leave multiple times during the year, subject to availability of the
       balance to be informed well in advance of at least 15 days of notice. However, such
       applicants must not violate the principle and purpose for which casual leave is provided.

   •   Leaves may be applied for a minimum of full days. There is no limit on the maximum
       number of days, subject to availability of balance.

   •   In a month, employees can avail maximum up to 5 days of Privilege leave.

   •   In a year, employees can avail maximum up to 12 days of Privilege leave.

   •   The leaves cannot be applied after availing the same, hence no back date leaves can be
       applied. If not applied prior may use his/her discretion to convert this into Loss of pay.

   •   If the employee applies Privilege Leave but does not avail of the same due to any reason,
       he/she may choose to cancel the same.

   •   The leave may be prefixed and or suffixed with weekends/statutory holidays. Intervening
       weekends and holidays are not counted as privilege leave days and cannot be combined with
       Maternity, Adoption, Paternity and Exam Leaves.

   •   The encashment formula is followed as mentioned below:
       Encashment amount = (last drawn basic salary of the last calendar year /number of days
       within a year) * eligible leave balance.

c) Special Scenarios:

   •   New Joined:

           1. The employee can avail leave if he/she has sufficient balance.

           2. Privilege leave is credited only after the employee has served his probation
              period.

   •   Employee goes on leave without pay (LWP):

       The employee is not entitled to leave when he/she is on leave without pay, hence there will be
       no leave of credit for the duration of the LWP.

   •   Employee serving notice period:

       The employee serving period cannot avail of Privilege leave at the time they have started
       serving the notice period.

   •   Employee Retirement:

       In case of retirement, the accumulated leave balance as of the date of retirement is encashed
       and paid to the employee in full and final accordance with the encashment formula.

   •   Employee Death:

       In case of death, the accumulated leave balance as of the date of death is encashed and paid to
       the nominee.

   •   Employee in Performance Improvement Plan (PIP):

       The employee in PIP cannot avail of Privilege leave at the time.

Terms and Conditions:

   •    There is a provision for an employee to apply for Advance Privileged leave which is that the
        employee has to inform the reporting manager/HR Department prior to 15 days of the leave
        to occur.

   •    During the leave period, the employee cannot take up any part-time or full-time employment
        for remuneration or otherwise, for any reason whatsoever.

   •    In case the leave exceeds the balance allotted in a month, it will result in a loss of
        pay, based on the HR manager’s discretion.

   •    In case the employee does not report back to his/her supervisor on the leave end date, the
        excess leave will be treated as unauthorized leave. Such unauthorized leave will be applied
        by HR and will result in a loss of pay.

   •    FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to initiate an exit procedure in case of the
        following:

                  ❖ The employee does not report back by the approved leave end date and does not
                    inform the supervisor.

                  ❖ Privilege Leave cannot be applied when in the notice period or in the
                    performance improvement Plan.

    •       These leaves can only be combined with Casual Leave, Floater Leave, and Bereavement
            Leave.

    •       Privilege Leave cannot be taken along with Paternity Leave, Maternity Leave, Exam
            Leave, or Adoption Leave.

    •       The leaves can be approved or rejected by the reporting manager or the HR Manager based
            on the project requirements.



Procedure

Applying for Leave:

        o     The employee can apply for leave through the Keka Portal.

        o     Login to KEKA-Go to Me section- Click on Leave- Apply for Leave.

        o     The employee completed the leave application form and submitted it for approval of the
              same.

        balance through the KEKA app.

              Manager and to the Branch Head.

    •   Employees can avail this leave with a maximum of 2 days at a time of a quarter.

    •   If an employee works a week off and wishes to avail compensatory leave, it must be taken

        compensatory leave.

    •   These leaves are credited to the employee on request only and shall be prior approved by the

c) Availing the Benefit

    •   This leave cannot be clubbed with any other type of leave.

    •   This leave should be informed and approved before availing the same.

    •   All the leave days in a request should be availed within a quarter; failure to the same will

       justification.

       inform the HR Department through email or the designated communication channel before

   This Policy is applicable to:

    •   All Full-time employees of FiftyFive Technologies Pvt

        the employee; personal emergency leaves wherein the employee may need additional time
        away from work. The company provides leave without pay for specific reasons and is

    •   These leaves are provided to extend support to employees during various life stages or during

    •   All LWP requests are subject to due approvals from the immediate reporting manager

Prevention of Sexual Harassment in The Workplace Policy

                          

  This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to
                        change any time as per the company policy.

Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited) Approved By:
            Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

PREVENTION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT


Introduction
This policy “Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy” has been framed in reference to the
requirement of “Sexual Harassment of Workmen at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition
and Redressal) Act, 2013” and rules framed thereunder (hereinafter referred to be as “the
Act”). Accordingly, this Policy covers all the important aspects of the Act and rules framed
thereunder. However, for any clarification, the respective provisions of the Act and rules shall
prevail over this Policy.

Objective
Our Company is committed to providing a work environment that ensures every employee is
treated with dignity and respect and afforded equitable treatment. The Company is also
committed to promoting a work environment that is conducive to the professional growth of
every employee and encourages equality of opportunity. The Company will not tolerate any
form of sexual harassment and is committed to taking all necessary steps to ensure that its
employees are not subjected to any form of harassment.

Scope
This Policy applies to all categories of employees of the Company, including permanent
management and workmen, temporaries, trainees, and employees on contract at its workplace
or at client sites. The Company will not tolerate sexual Harassment if engaged in by clients
suppliers, or any other business associates.

The workplace includes:

    •   All offices or other premises where the Company’s business is conducted in the
        ordinary course.
    •   All company-related activities performed at any other site away from the Company’s
        premises.
    •   Any place visited by the employee arising out of or during the course of
        employment including transportation provided by the employer for undertaking such
        journey.

1. Definition of Sexual Harassment –
According to Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and
Redressal) Act, 2013, Sexual Harassment includes any one or more of the following
unwelcome acts or behavior(whether directly or by implication) namely:
    ● physical contact and advances; or
    ● a demand or request for sexual favor; or
    ● making sexually colored remarks; or
    ● showing pornography; or
    ● any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature;

The Sexual harassment is “an unacceptable conduct of a sexual nature, or other conduct based
on sex abuse affecting the dignity of men or women at work”. Sexual harassment will
generally be unwanted, unreasonable or offensive or it may be a combination of all three. It
may cause the employee who is being harassed to feel threatened or humiliated. It may
interfere with the employee’s job performance, undermine job security or create a threatening
or intimidating working environment. Although the word “harassment” has connotations of
repeated conduct, an employee can be harassed by a single act. Sexual harassment can consist
of several different types of behavior, some of which are more obvious than others. This list is
not exhaustive but,

for example:-

    ● Sexual harassment can take the form of gestures or leering,
    ● Sending letters,
    ● Gifts or offensive publications or the use of pin-ups
    ● Unwanted jokes, gestures, offensive words on clothing, and unwelcome comments and
      repartee
    ● Touching and any other bodily contact such as scratching or patting a coworker's
        back, grabbing an employee around the waist, or interfering with an employee's
        ability to move.
    ● Repeated requests for dates that are turned down or unwanted flirting
    ● Transmitting or posting emails or pictures of a sexual or other harassment-related
      nature.
    ● Displaying sexually suggestive objects, pictures, or posters.
    ● Playing sexually suggestive music.

Alternatively, sexual harassment may consist of spoken comments, including unwanted
propositions, jokes of a sexual nature, questions or comments of a sexual nature or the
suggestion that an employee’s career can be 2 advanced by bestowing sexual favors (or
alternatively that an employee’s career will be damaged if they do not accede to sexual
requests). A third sort of sexual harassment involves physical contact including “accidental”
contact, or deliberate patting, fondling or groping.



2. Internal Complaints Committee:
The Company has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee (“ICC”) in accordance with
the Section 4of the Act. The Committee is constituted at all administrative units or offices for
redressal of sexual harassment complaint (made by the victim) and for ensuring time bound
treatment of such complaints.


                                    Internal Complaints Committee




          Presiding Officer -                                               Head of Human
          Senior Women &                                                    Resources of the
           Men Employee                                                        Company



Following are the members of the committee:


                                              Role
                                       Presiding Officer
                                       Presiding Officer
                                           Head HR


At the time of inquiry, Minimum 3 members including Presiding Officer shall be present. The
group shall include the Presiding Officer and at least three members, one-half of whom shall
be women.

3. Redressal Process
   A. Any employee who feels and is being sexually harassed directly or indirectly may
        submit a complaint of the alleged incident to any member of the Committee in writing
        with his/her signature within 3 Months of occurrence of incident. The Internal
        Complaint Committee may extend the time limit for a reasonable cause. Complaint
        shall be submitted in six copies along with supporting documents and the names and
        address of witnesses.
   B. If a complaint cannot be made in writing, the Committee shall provide reasonable
        assistance to the employee for making the complaint in writing.
   C. If the aggrieved employee is unable to make a complaint, then any of her legal heir
        may make a complaint on his/ her behalf.
   D. The committee shall send one copy of complaint to the respondent within a period of 7
        days and respondent shall file his reply within a period of 10 days.
   E. The committee at the request of the aggrieved employee shall take the steps to settle
        the case through conciliation without involving any monetary settlement as a basis of
        conciliation and where the settlement has been arrived, no inquiry shall be conducted.
   F. In case, respondent is an employee, the committee shall, proceed to make an inquiry in
        accordance with the provisions of service rules applicable to the respondent or other
        prescribed rules and in case of domestic worker, the local committee shall forward the
        complaint to the police within 7 (Seven) days for registering the case under Indian
        Penal Code, 1860, except for those cases which has been arrived for settlement as
        mentioned in point (5) above.
   G. The inquiry shall be completed within a period of 90 days.
   H. The committee shall provide a report of findings to the employer within 10 days of
        completion of inquiry and also to the concerned parties and opportunity of being
        heard shall also be given to them.
   I.   If an allegation against the respondent has been proved, the committee shall
        recommend to the employer.

J. In case, the complaint is found to be false, the Complainant shall, if deemed fit, be
    liable for appropriate disciplinary action by the Management but a mere inability to
    substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the
    Complainant.
           i. to take adequate action for sexual harassment as a misconduct in accordance
              with the provisions of the service rules applicable to the respondent;
          ii. to deduct, notwithstanding anything in the service rules applicable to the
              respondent, from the salary or wages of the respondent such sum as it may
              consider appropriate.


K. If the Complainant was aggrieved from the recommendation made by Committee to
    employer then he/she may prefer appeal to the appellate authority notified under
    clause (a) of Section 2 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946.
L. The Committee will maintain a register to endorse the complaint received by it and
    keep the contents confidential, if it is so desired, except to use the same for discreet
    investigation.
M. The Committee will hold a meeting with the Complainant within five days of the
    receipt of the complaint, but no later than a week in any case.
N. At the first meeting, the Committee members shall hear the Complainant and record
    her/his allegations. The Complainant can also submit any corroborative material with
    a documentary proof, oral or written material, etc., to substantiate his/ her complaint.
    If the Complainant does not wish to depose personally due to embarrassment of
    narration of the event, a lady officer for lady employees involved and a male officer
    for male employees involved shall meet and record the statement.
O. Thereafter, the person against whom a complaint is made may be called for a
    deposition before the Committee and an opportunity will be given to him/ her to give
    an explanation, where after, an “Enquiry” shall be conducted and concluded.
P. In the event, the complaint does not fall under the purview of Sexual Harassment or the
    complaint does not mean an offence of Sexual Harassment, the same would be
    dropped after recording the reasons thereof in writing.

4. Enquiry Process
   A. The Committee shall immediately proceed with the Enquiry and communicate the
      same to the Complainant and the person against whom the complaint is made
   B. The Committee shall prepare and hand over the Statement of Allegation to the
      person against whom the complaint is made and give him/ her an opportunity to
      submit a written explanation if he/ she so desires within 7 days of receipt of the
      same.
   C. The Complainant shall be provided with a copy of the written explanation
      submitted by the person against whom complaint is made.
   D. If the Complainant or the person against whom complaint is made desires any
      witness/es to be called, they shall communicate in writing to the Committee the
      names of witness/es whom they propose to call.
   E. If the Complainant desires to tender any documents by way of evidence before the
      Committee, she/ he shall supply original copies of such documents. Similarly, if
      the person against whom a complaint is made desires to tender any documents in
      evidence before the Committee she/ he shall supply original copies of such
      documents.
   F. The Committee shall call upon all witnesses mentioned by both the parties.
   G. The Committee shall provide every reasonable opportunity to the Complainant and
      to the person against whom complaint is made, for putting forward and defending
      their respective case.
   H. The Committee shall complete the “Enquiry” within a reasonable period but not
      beyond three months and communicate its findings and its recommendations for
      action to the HR . The report of the committee shall be treated as an enquiry report
      on the basis of which an erring employee can be awarded appropriate 4
      punishment straightaway.
   I. The HR will direct appropriate action in accordance with the recommendation
      proposed by the Committee.
   J. The Committee shall be governed by such rules as may be framed by the Supreme
      Court orders or any other legislation enacted later on.

6. Other Points to be considered
    A. The Committee may recommend the VP-HR action which may include transfer or
        any of the other appropriate disciplinary action.
    B. The management shall provide all necessary assistance for the purpose of ensuring
        full, effective and speedy implementation of this Policy.
    C. Where sexual harassment occurs as a result of an act or omission by any third party
        or outsider, TPC shall take all steps necessary and reasonable to assist the affected
        person in terms of support and preventive action.
    D. The Committee shall analyze and put up a report on all complaints of this nature at
        the end of the year for submission to VP- HR.
    E. In case, the Committee finds the degree of offense coverable under the Indian
        Penal Code, then these facts shall be mentioned in its report and appropriate action
        shall be initiated by the Management, for making a Police Complaint.


Actions against Harassment can Include:-
    ● Written disciplinary warnings
    ● Demotion
    ● Suspension
    ● Termination


7. Confidentiality
The Company understands that it is difficult for the victim to come forward with a
complaint of sexual harassment and recognizes the victim’s interest in keeping the matter
confidential. To protect the interests of the victim, the accused person and others who may
report incidents of sexual harassment, confidentiality will be maintained throughout the
investigatory process to the extent practicable and appropriate under the circumstances.
The contents of complaint, the identity and addresses of the aggrieved woman, respondent
and witnesses, any information relating to conciliation and inquiry proceedings,
recommendations of the Internal Committee and the action taken by the employer shall
not be published, communicated or made known to the public, press and media in any
manner.


8. Access to Reports And Documents

All records of complaints, including contents of meetings, results of investigations and
other relevant material will be kept confidential by the Company except where disclosure
is required under disciplinary or other remedial processes.

Employee Referral Policy


Introduction
This Employee Referral Policy outlines the framework for encouraging employees of FiftyFive
Technologies to recommend suitable candidates for open positions within the organization. The policy
defines the process, eligibility, and reward structure for employee referrals, aiming to support efficient
talent acquisition while maintaining fairness, transparency, and cost-effective hiring practices.



Objective
To define the procedures and guidelines for rewarding employees of FiftyFive Technologies who
contribute to identifying and attracting suitable and competent talent, in order to meet organizational
resource requirements in a timely and cost-effective manner.



Eligibility
   ● All current employees of FiftyFive Technologies including trainees on rolls of the Company are
     covered under this policy.

   ● The referral Policy hence is not applicable for the HR department as it is to be considered that
     they are a part of hiring procedures.

   ● The referral policy is not applicable for the freelancers/ part timers in the company.

Procedure
   ● Employees may refer individuals who fit the specifications given in job descriptions for vacant
     positions which Human Resources posts from time to time.

        Note: If the referred candidate’s resume is already available in the Company’s database or
        has been referred earlier through another source, the referral will be considered on a first-
        come, first-served basis. Duplicate referrals will not be eligible for referral incentives.

   ● The employee’s role will be limited to the submission of the resume of the candidate. After this
     the regular process of short listing and interviews will be applied to the referrals also.

   ● The employee making the referral will not in any way be involved with the interview or salary
     fixation of the candidate.

   ● Selection of referred candidates by any employee would be made only after going through the
     selection process, as per recruitment policy / procedures.

   ● There should be no specific canvassing in case of a referred candidate by both the employee
     who referred him and the HR.

   ● If the preferred candidate is hired, the referrer is eligible to claim a referral fee as per the
     parameters defined below:



Parameters

                          Grade
                                                             Bracket                   INR

         Associate Technical Lead/Senior

                                                          1 Years-4 Years              15,000

               ● The incentive will be credited to the employee only if the new recruit completes 3

               ● Incentive amounts and eligibility factors are subject to change based on the
                 business and economic needs of FiftyFive Technologies.

               ● Incentive will be applicable only on the first come first served.

               ● COMPANY, will not enter into any debate with an employee who has
                 unsuccessfully referred a personal contact. In the event of any dispute, the decision
                 of the Head of Human Resources shall be final.

               ● All recommendations made by the company’s employees must come from their
                 personal contacts / connections and not through any recruitment agency.

               ● Referral bonus is not applicable for the employees working in the human resources

SEPARATION POLICY


Introduction
FiftyFive has a mandatory Separation Policy that every employee who leaves FiftyFive Technologies
needs to undergo. The Separation Policy enables the employees to understand their roles, and
responsibilities and follow them as per FiftyFive’s expected policy standards.



Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to introduce the employee to separation with FiftyFive Technologies.



Applicability
This policy is applicable to all the Interns/Full-Time Employees and Contractual Employees
of FiftyFive Technologies.



Provisions:


Employee separation refers to the conclusion of an individual’s employment relationship with the
Company. Depending on the circumstances, separation may be initiated by the employee, by the
Company, or may occur due to other specified events. The Company classifies employee separation under
the following types:

    1. Employee Initiated Separation (Resignation)

TRAVEL POLICY

Purpose
This document provides guidelines and establishes procedures for employees incurring business travel
and entertainment expenses on the company’s behalf.



Objective

     • To ensure all employees have a clear and consistent understanding of policies and procedures for
        business travel and entertainment.

     • To provide business travelers with a reasonable level of service and comfort at the most cost-
        effective level.

     • To maximize the company’s ability to negotiate discounted rates with preferred suppliers and
        reduce travel expenses.



Scope
This travel policy applies to all employees of FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Ltd and all those traveling on
behalf of FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Ltd.

 1. Responsibility and Applicability
    The traveler is responsible for complying with the travel policy. The approver is responsible for
    accurately reviewing expense reports for compliance.

          ● The company will reimburse employees for all reasonable and necessary expenses while
            traveling on authorized company business.

          ● The travel should be approved and informed to the HR department prior to at least one
            month.

          ● The company assumes no obligation to reimburse employees for expenses that are not in
            compliance with this policy. Travelers who do not comply with this travel policy may be
            subject to:

                    ❖ Delay or withholding of reimbursement
                    ❖ Disciplinary action
                    ❖ This Policy is applicable to all employees who are traveling in terms of business
                      purpose only on behalf of the requirement claimed by the company.

 2. Who to Call on Travel Policy Issues:

    Any questions, concerns or suggestions regarding this travel policy may be directed to the HR
    department of FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Ltd.



General Guidelines to be followed in the policy:

    • A travel request must be approved before proceeding on any international or domestic travel.

    • Any international or domestic travel request must be raised and followed as per the company
      travel policy and procedure.

    • If there is any change in the travel (domestic or international) due to any reason and it is more
      costly than the approval that has already been taken, a fresh travel request needs to be raised in
      this case.

    • Any employee who requires traveling for business purposes must get approval in advance from
      the reporting manager and the head of the human resources department.

    • An email needs to be sent to the finance and human resource department along with approval mail
      to get the travel advance.

    • Most economical modes of travel and fastest route to the destination would be reimbursed.

    • Food expenses are allowed only as per the limit of entitlements.

    • No expense will be reimbursed for alcoholic beverages or cigarettes etc.

    • The expense report with travel requests submitted to the finance department must consist of the
      original boarding pass and travel -tickets. Any deviation from the tour program shall be approved
      by the reporting manager and the head of the human resources department.

Traveling By Air:
Employees are expected to take the lowest airfare and fastest route to the destination while
traveling. The undermentioned guidelines to be followed while traveling by air for the company's
business purpose.

         ● There should not be more than 1 stoppage in case of domestic travel.

         ● As per the Company travel policy any exception needs to have approval from the
           reporting manager and the head of human resources department.

         ● Any kind of additional fee which is occurring due to any reason like seat upgradation etc.
           will not be included.

         ● All ticket bookings need to be initiated by the Human Resources Department and shall be
           approved prior to the bookings from the Finance Department.



         a) Class to be Chosen

               ●   While on air travel, organization employees are expected to fly in the economy
                   class which comes under the category of economical fare. Business class is
                   allowed only for management level and above.

               ●   All policy exceptions must be noted on the travel request form and must be
                   approved in advance by the management and above level.

               ●   In case any rebooking is done, it must be reimbursed in case of emergency only.



        b) Cancellation of Traveling:

        In case of any cancellation done to the already planned business trip, the employee must
        inform the travel help desk who in turn will check from the carrier if the ticket can be
        refunded.

Rail Transportation

    ● Rail transportation can be availed by the employee in case travel distance is less than 12
        hours.

    ● Rail transportation must be done in the most economical way and with the fastest route of
        travel only with prior approval from the reporting manager and the head of the Human
        Resources Department.

    ● Bookings need to be initiated by the Human Resources Department only with prior approval
        to the Finance Department.



Lodging
Using the “Corporate travel policy " the organization has tie-ups with different hotels.

    ● The bookings will be taken care strictly by the HR team and the details will be shared
      accordingly to the respective employee official mail ID.

    ● Any exception in terms of hotel stay must be approved by the reporting manager and the Head
      of Human Resources department. before the start of travel.

    ● In case of non-compliance with the travel policy, the extra amount paid will be bearable by
      the employee.



Reimbursement of Meal and Conveyance Expense
The reimbursement of the travel expense will be done on the basis of below mentioned points:

   - Meals Expenses:
      The company policy states that expenditure incurred on meals (breakfast, lunch or dinner) will
      be reimbursed while the employee is on business travel up to INR 700 per person in a day.


   - Cabs Expenses:
        ●    The company policy states that expenditure incurred on travel from the destined hotel to
             office location in Jaipur/Gurgaon/Indore will be reimbursed while the employee is on
             business travel upto INR 200 per person in a day.

The process to raise travel request:
           •   The process to be followed by an employee while going on domestic travel as per
               travel policy template is explained below.

           •   If any team is planning to travel for the business requirements, The Travel Request
               Form needs to be filled out promptly. To streamline the process, the Reporting
               Manager (RM) will fill out the Travel Form on behalf of the entire team & will get
               signed by the HR Manager.

           •   It is mandatory for employees traveling for official purposes to complete the Travel
               Request Form . The form must be filled out by the employee and signed by both the
               Reporting Manager & HR Manager before the trip is undertaken .

           •   Employees have to submit the actual bills in KEKA however if any changes are
               highlighted separately.

PROVISIONS (what is not included in travel policy):

      1. Gatherings or outings organized spontaneously by team members for team-building
         purposes may not fall under the official travel policy.

      2. Travel for personal events such as weddings, family reunions, or other non-business events
         will not be covered under the Travel Policy.

      3. If any team, along with the Reporting Manager, requires employees to report to the office
         for a specific duration to fulfill team requirements will not be covered under the travel
         policy . Such instances fall outside the scope of travel reimbursement of allowances.



Right to Amend Policies

This Employee Handbook is intended to provide general guidance on Company policies and practices.
FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to amend, modify, suspend, or withdraw any policy,
procedure, or benefit described in this handbook at any time, with or without notice, based on
business, operational, or legal requirements.

AI Ethics Policy

Our organization is committed to the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence. We ensure
that all AI systems are designed and deployed with fairness, transparency, and accountability. Bias
in data and models is actively monitored and mitigated to promote equitable outcomes for all users.


We prioritize data privacy and security in every AI-driven solution. Personal and sensitive
information is handled in compliance with applicable regulations, and strict access controls are
maintained. AI systems are continuously audited to ensure they operate within defined ethical and
legal boundaries.


Human oversight remains central to all AI implementations. Decisions made by AI systems are
subject to review, and mechanisms are in place to allow users to challenge or appeal outcomes.
We strive to build AI solutions that enhance human capabilities while maintaining trust and integrity.
